red_star_rosette_1.description: A six-pointed star rosette drawn in red ink, located in the left margin outside the main text column. Consists of six pointed lobes radiating from a central circle, with red pigment applied throughout. These stars are the defining decorative feature of this folio and are consistent with the Astronomical/Stars section designation ($I=S). This star sits at the topmost position, flanking lines f116r.1–2. Star decorations do not encroach on the text column — they occupy negative space to the left of x~105.

red_star_rosette_2.description: Second red six-pointed star rosette in the left margin, flanking approximately lines f116r.5–6. Identical form to star 1 but slightly smaller in rendering. Consistent spacing from the text body left edge (~x=105).

red_star_rosette_3.description: Third red six-pointed star rosette in the left margin, flanking approximately lines f116r.9–10. The red ink appears slightly more faded on this star compared to stars 1 and 2, consistent with differential pigment preservation.

red_star_rosette_4.description: Fourth red six-pointed star rosette in the left margin, flanking approximately lines f116r.12–13. This is the last star in the upper paragraph block. Its lower edge is approximately at y=320, just above the inter-paragraph gap.

red_star_rosette_5.description: Fifth red six-pointed star rosette in the left margin, flanking approximately lines f116r.16–17. This star is the first of the lower paragraph block's marginal decorations. It is visually slightly larger than stars 3–4.

red_star_rosette_6.description: Sixth and final red six-pointed star rosette in the left margin, flanking approximately lines f116r.20–21. After this star, no further marginal star decorations are observed for the remaining ~30 lines of the folio. The absence of further stars in the lower two-thirds of the lower block may indicate a visual section end or that additional stars were planned but not executed.

inter_paragraph_gap.description: A distinct horizontal gap in the text body visible between line f116r.14 (which ends the upper paragraph block) and line f116r.15 (which begins the lower block with a 'p'-initial gallows glyph). The gap is approximately 30–40 normalized units tall (y~340–375). This is the only text-free horizontal zone within the central text body of the folio. No illustration or decoration fills this gap — it is a pure scribal section break.

gallows_glyph_line1.description: The tall ascending 'k'-initial gallows glyph at the very start of f116r.1, the @P0 paragraph opener. This character extends significantly above the normal line cap height, functioning as a visual paragraph marker. Its vertical stroke is approximately 40 normalized units tall.

folio_number_annotation.description: The Arabic numeral '116' written in a later (post-medieval) hand at the top-right of the parchment. This is a modern archival folio number, not part of the original manuscript. Written in darker brown ink over the parchment edge area.

left_margin_ruling_line.description: A faint vertical scoring or dry-point ruling line along the left text boundary at approximately x=105. This is the left margin guide that all text lines in the folio align to. It is most visible under raking light analysis and is consistent with standard medieval manuscript preparation.

text_blocks_mapping.description: The upper paragraph block comprising lines f116r.1 through f116r.14. This block begins with an @P0 paragraph-start locus and ends at the short terminal line f116r.14. It occupies the upper approximately 34% of the parchment text area (y~18–340). Six red star rosette decorations flank this block in the left margin at regular intervals (approximately every 2–3 lines). No <-> bisections occur in this block — text runs full-width from left margin (x~105) to right margin (x~940). Lines are densely packed with approximately 18–22 normalized units of vertical spacing per line.

isolated_zones.description: Red star rosette 1 (x:28–100, y:30–80) is entirely within the left margin zone to the left of the ruling line at x~105. It does not interact with any text glyph. The 5-normalized-unit gap between the star's right edge (~x=100) and the text left margin (x~105) is maintained consistently across all six rosettes, confirming deliberate spatial separation. The star is purely decorative and has no transcription locus.

Red star rosette 2 (x:28–100, y:115–165) flanks lines f116r.4–5 but is entirely left of the text column. No text wraps around it. The consistent vertical spacing between rosettes (~85–90 normalized units center-to-center) suggests they were drawn at regular pre-measured intervals.

Red star rosette 3 (x:28–100, y:205–255) flanks lines f116r.7–9. Entirely in the left margin. The slightly faded red ink of this rosette compared to rosettes 1–2 suggests differential pigment aging or a different application thickness.

Red star rosette 4 (x:28–100, y:270–320) flanks lines f116r.11–12. This is the last star of the upper block. Its lower edge at y~320 is approximately 20 normalized units above the last dense lines of block A (lines 11–14 at y~318–436).

Red star rosette 5 (x:28–100, y:360–410) bridges the inter_paragraph_gap zone (y~437–475) and the beginning of lower block B. It was likely drawn before the text was written in this section, as its vertical positioning slightly anticipates the actual start of block B at y~477.

Red star rosette 6 (x:28–100, y:455–505) is the final marginal star decoration. After this point (~y=505 and below), no further star rosettes appear for the remaining ~36 lines of the folio. The absence of further stars may indicate: (a) the planned star-series ended here, (b) additional stars were intended but not drawn, or (c) the marginal star decorations were applied to mark specific textual sections and the lower block required no further sectional marking.

The inter_paragraph_gap (x:105–950, y~437–475) is the only text-free horizontal zone within the central text body of f116r. It is approximately 38 normalized units tall. No illustration, decoration, or annotation fills this space. The gap is consistent with a deliberate scribal section break, dividing the folio into upper block A (14 lines) and lower block B (36 lines). The gap is narrower than typical inter-paragraph gaps in the herbal section, suggesting the scribe was conserving parchment space.
